Definition: properly, to pour out (transitive or intransitive); by implication, to melt or cast as metal; by extension, to place firmly, to stiffen or grow hard
BiblicalUsage: Yâtsaq means to pour out, and so to cast metal in a mould. Samuel poured oil on Saul's head and anointed him captain over God's inheritance, and the chapiters of the temple pillars were of molten brass, poured and set in place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God pours out His Spirit as oil, and the anointing makes a king of a farmer's son.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
